text_blocks.snippet: Treatment options for hypertension (high blood pressure) combine lifestyle changes and prescription medications to lower blood pressure and protect against heart disease, stroke, and kidney damage.
snippet_highlighted_words: combine lifestyle changes and prescription medications

text_blocks.snippet: Doctors recommend heart-healthy lifestyle changes for all people with high blood pressure, and sometimes these changes are enough to control stage 1 hypertension:

list.snippet: Diet: Follow the DASH Eating Plan, which focuses on fruits, vegetables, whole grains, low-fat dairy, and low sodium (salt) intake.
Weight Management: Lose extra body weight or maintain a healthy weight to reduce the workload on your heart.
Physical Activity: Get regular aerobic exercise, such as brisk walking, cycling, or swimming.
Habits: Quit smoking or using tobacco, and limit alcohol intake (no more than one drink per day for women and two for men).
Sleep & Stress: Aim for at least 7 hours of quality sleep per night and manage stress levels.

text_blocks.snippet: When lifestyle changes do not lower blood pressure sufficiently—or if you have a high cardiovascular risk, diabetes, or kidney disease—healthcare providers prescribe one or more Types of Blood Pressure Medications:

list.snippet: Thiazide Diuretics: "Water pills" that help your body get rid of excess sodium and water.
ACE Inhibitors (Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme Inhibitors): Medications like lisinopril that relax and widen blood vessels.
ARBs (Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers): Medications like losartan that block the action of chemicals that narrow blood vessels.
Calcium Channel Blockers (CCBs): Medications like amlodipine that prevent calcium from entering heart and blood vessel muscle cells to let vessels relax.
Other Options: Beta-blockers, alpha-blockers, or central-acting agents may be added depending on specific heart conditions or if you have Resistant Hypertension.
Renal Denervation: A minimally invasive, FDA-approved procedure that can help lower blood pressure in patients with uncontrolled or resistant hypertension who do not respond well to medications.
